channel.title: AI Price Watch — daily AI model price moves
channel.description: What every AI model costs per million tokens, and what moved today. Feeds an AI cost audit: I track the prices, you keep 70% of what I cut.

item.title: The professionals arrived — AI spend is now a funded category
item.description:
Same model, same day, opposite directions. Of 41 price changes logged today across 465 models, 24 were cuts and 11 were rises — but the biggest riser and the biggest news sit on the same row. Z.ai's GLM 5.2 input went $0.171 → $0.62 (+933%) on the same day its output fell $7.00 → $2.42 (-65.4%). Input up nine times, output down two-thirds, one model, one afternoon. Its input had fallen 82.5% on 8 Oct, so today it completed a full round trip in eight days.

The floor from Monday got taken back. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash input went $0.0238 → $0.15 (+530%) — that is the same model the 13 Oct brief called the cheap floor after a 70.6% cut. DeepSeek Pro Latest output rose +90.9%, GLM 5.3 Flash output +80%. The cuts went to other doors: GLM 5.3 Flash input $0.15 → $0.0113 (-92.5%), DeepSeek Pro Latest output $8.00 → $0.7484 (-90.6%), Meta's Llama 3.3 70B input -83.1%.

The churn is now the headline. The log holds 31 round trips — models that fell more than 20% and climbed straight back — up from 20 yesterday. GLM 5.2 input is the biggest: down 82.5% on 8 Oct, up 933% today. Every round trip, live →

And the money noticed. Today alone: North.cloud raised a $60M Series B to keep runaway cloud and AI costs in check, Ramp closed $1.85B at a $60B valuation and expanded into AI spend management, HubSpot added AI credit caps and pay-as-you-go (15 Oct) and Accenture put a monthly cap on employee Claude usage. The category just got funded — for enterprises. An SMB spending $2k/month still has a spreadsheet, a renewal date, and nobody who will re-cost it against prices that moved 41 times today.

Concretely: 200M input / 40M output on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cost $4.76/month of input on 15 Oct and $30.00 today — five days after it was called the cheap floor. Re-cost your exact model, run your spend, or book the free clinic.

item.title: The floor snapped back — the same +305% hike, three days later
item.description:
The cheap tier re-inflated, and it is the second time this week. Of 41 price changes logged today across 461 models, 28 were increases. OpenAI's gpt-oss-120b went $0.037 → $0.15 input (+305%) and $0.17 → $0.60 output (+253%) — the identical move it made on 13 Oct, which was fully reverted on 14 Oct and is now back on. Qwen3.8 27B input went $0.04 → $0.24 (+500%), giving back the 90% floor-cut of 11 Oct. Z.ai's GLM 5.3 input rose +316% and +406% on two routes; Gemma 4 31B input +122%.

The cuts did not stop. Moonshot's Kimi Latest input fell 45.9% ($0.536 → $0.29), GLM 5.3 Flash output 44.4%, Kimi K3 input 35.7%, GLM 5.1 27.4% both sides, DeepSeek Flash output 19.2%. Cheap capacity is still there — just not where it was on Monday.

The point is not the direction, it is the churn. The log now holds 20 round trips — a model that fell more than 20% and climbed straight back inside the window. The biggest is Qwen3.8 27B input: down 90% on 11 Oct, up 500% on 15 Oct. A bill costed on a monthly snapshot is now wrong in both directions. See every round trip, live →

Concretely: 200M input / 40M output on gpt-oss-120b cost $14.20/month on 12 Oct, $54.00 on 13 Oct, $14.20 on 14 Oct, and $54.00 again today. Same workload, same week. Re-cost your exact model or run your spend.

item.title: The cheap tier tripled overnight — 15 rises, 4 cuts
item.description:
The models built for cost got 3x more expensive in one night. gpt-oss-120b — the open workhorse a lot of self-hosted and agent stacks default to — moved from $0.037 in / $0.17 out to $0.15 in / $0.60 out: +305% on input and +253% on output. Meta's Llama 3.3 70B input rose 168% ($0.22 → $0.59). MiniMax M2.7 rose 43% on both sides. DeepSeek Flash Latest output jumped 373% ($0.1332 → $0.63). Of 22 changes logged today, 15 were increases — the second straight day risers beat cuts, and this time it hit the cheap end hardest.

The floor still exists, just elsewhere. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cut input 70.6% ($0.15 → $0.0441) and keeps $0.63 output. GLM 5.3 Flash output fell 25% ($1.20 → $0.90, with its input up 12.5%). Meta also listed Muse Wonder at $20.00 output — a premium tier landing on the same page as four-cent input.

Concretely: a workload of 200M input / 40M output that cost $14.20/month on gpt-oss-120b yesterday costs $54.00 today. The same volume on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash costs $34.02. Nothing about the workload changed. Only the default did.

That is the whole reason a monthly re-cost matters: the models priced for "cheap" are the ones that moved most, and a default set last month is now either bleeding or wrongly routed. Scan your exact model and volume, or run your spend.

item.title: The floor stopped falling — 12 cuts, 13 rises
item.description:
Half the market went up overnight. Of 25 price changes logged in the last day, 13 were increases. Z.ai's GLM 5.3 Flash output jumped 140% ($0.50 → $1.20) while its input fell 84.5% ($0.15 → $0.0232) in the same move. DeepSeek V4 Pro 0423 more than doubled input and output (+108.8%). Meta's Llama 4 Scout output rose 96.7% ($0.30 → $0.59). The floor is still dropping on other routes — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cut 50% to $0.15 in / $0.60 out — but not on everything.

That is the whole reason a fixed default is dangerous: two models from the same lab moved in opposite directions on the same night. Whatever your AI bill was costed on is now wrong in one direction or the other — and nobody re-checks it.

The cheap routes still exist: the cheapest input tracked here is now $0.0128/1M tokens (DeepSeek V4 Flash Latest), the cheapest output $0.03 (Mistral Nemo). Run your number, and I'll find which of your lines moved.

item.title: The input floor just fell 90%
item.description:
Ten cuts in one day, and the cheapest input on this page now costs four cents. Qwen3.8 27B input fell 90.6% ($0.425 → $0.04 per million tokens) and DeepSeek Flash output fell 76.8% ($0.60 → $0.14) overnight — logged live in the table below. DeepSeek V4 Flash output halved again (−50%), Kimi K3 output fell 25.9%. Whatever your AI bill was costed on, the market moved underneath it while you slept.

The money side stayed blunt the same week: OpenAI's annualised revenue landed roughly $20B below plan (TechCrunch / FT, 8 Oct) and analysts now say AI revenue has to reach $400–600B by 2027 to avoid a spending cliff (Barron's, 9 Oct). Cheaper models, louder ROI questions.

Both halves sit side by side on this page: the invoice is under scrutiny, and the cheaper price already exists. Run your number, and I'll find the cut.

item.title: Spend scrutiny
item.description:
The AI trade just got repriced — and so did the excuse to overspend. OpenAI's annualised revenue landed roughly $20B below what investors had been told (CNBC, 8 Oct), and AI stocks sold off on the report. Translation for anyone signing the AI invoice: "budget by vibes" is over, and CFOs are auditing the line right now.

The model market cut again overnight on the same page: DeepSeek V4 Flash output down 97.3%, Z.ai GLM Flash output down 92.6%, Qwen3.5-35B input down 46.7% — logged in the table below.

item.title: Price war
item.description:
The frontier tier just repriced. Anthropic shipped Claude Haiku 5.5 and OpenAI shipped GPT-6. On the market this page reads, Haiku 5.5 lists at $0.10 in / $0.50 out per million tokens — an order of magnitude under Haiku 4.5 at $1.00 / $5.00 — with a 1M-token context. OpenAI's new GPT-6 "luna" tier lands at the same $0.10 / $0.50.

Open-weight prices slid again in the same window: DeepSeek V4 Flash input down 66.7%, GLM 5.2 input down 82.5%, DeepSeek Pro input down 62.2% — logged in the table below. If your AI bill was costed on last year's prices, it is now priced against a market that has moved underneath it.
